growth_story.headline: Macao's gaming boom lifted income per person to a 2013 peak; a VIP slump and the pandemic left it 32.9 percent lower in 2025.
growth_story.arc: Income per person in Macao grew slowly in 1990–1997, at 1.4 percent a year, and faster in 1998–2005, at 5.4 percent a year. The fastest era, 2006–2013 at 9.3 percent a year, followed the opening of the gaming sector to outside investment in 2002 and a sharp rise in visitors from Mainland China, and it carried income per person to its peak in 2013. The boom ended in 2014 as high-stakes VIP gambling fell during an anti-corruption campaign on the Mainland, and income per person dropped 24.3 percent in 2015. The pandemic then cut off visitors: income per person fell 55.3 percent in 2020 and bounced back 74.9 percent in 2023 after Mainland China lifted its controls. Across 2014–2025 growth averaged 1.1 percent a year, and in 2025 income per person was still 32.9 percent below the 2013 peak, about where it first was in 2010.

threads.title: Casinos open, mainland visitors arrive
threads.text: Macao is the only place in China where casino gambling is legal. The IMF links the long boom after 1999 to that monopoly, to the opening of gaming to outside investors in 2002, and to fast-rising spending power on the Mainland, which brought a sharp rise in mainland visitors. This is the background to the 9.3 percent a year growth of 2006–2013.

threads.title: The VIP gaming slump
threads.text: From 2014 the high-stakes VIP side of the casino business shrank fast and gaming exports fell sharply. The IMF ties this to a wider fall in luxury spending and the anti-corruption campaign on the Mainland. Income per person fell in 2014, 2015 and 2016.

threads.title: Pandemic closure and reopening
threads.text: When visitors stopped coming in 2020, Macao's exports of services collapsed and income per person fell 55.3 percent. The sharp rebound came in 2023, after Mainland China lifted its COVID-19 controls.

threads.title: Uneven recovery, weak private investment
threads.text: Tourists have returned, but gaming revenue has not regained its pre-pandemic peak. The IMF describes private investment held back by tight credit, a slow property market and unspent public budgets.

since_last_year.text: Growth stayed positive in 2025, with income per person up 4.8 percent, led by gaming and tourism. In July 2026 IMF staff reported that tourist arrivals had passed pre-pandemic levels, while gaming revenue was still below its earlier peak and private investment was held back by tight credit.

growth_story.tension: The IMF describes a recovery in which tourist arrivals have passed pre-pandemic levels, but income per person in 2025 was still below its 2019 level and 32.9 percent under the 2013 peak. The 4.4 percent a year average for 2016–2025 is lifted by the 74.9 percent rebound in 2023, which made up only part of the 55.3 percent fall in 2020; the era since 2014 averages 1.1 percent.
